_readme: Fixture corpus for src/eval/groundedness.py (WO-A16, ADR 0074).
Hand-authored, not recorded. This repository has no offline sample of
real arXiv PDF text and fetching one is what the harness forbids, so
the paper prose below is original. What is NOT invented is the set of
extraction artefacts planted in `pdf_text`: each is a code point a
TeX-set arXiv PDF genuinely extracts as, and each has its own test in
tests/test_groundedness.py.
Artefacts planted in pdf_text, and where:
U+FB01 / U+FB00  ligatures      'fine-tuned', 'differs', 'effect'
'-' + newline    hyphenation    'inter-\nnational'
U+00AD           soft hyphen    'post-hoc \u00adfilter'
U+201C/U+201D    curly quotes   'closed-book'
U+2013 / U+2014  en / em dash   '12.4\u2013point', results sentence
U+00A0           no-break space 'benchmark\u00a0suite'
U+200B           zero width sp. 'we measured\u200b'
U+000C           page break     between sections 1 and 2
papers/citations are ResearchState shapes (src/graph/state.py).
paper 2401.00003 deliberately has NO pdf_text: it is the source-
incomplete case, where a quote cannot be falsified and must leave the
denominator rather than fail.
No PDF is fetched, parsed or written by any test that reads this file.
reports: grounded (everything resolves), hallucinated (a citation the
run never retrieved, a malformed id, a near-miss quote and a quote
attributed to the wrong paper), quiet (no quotations at all), and
partial_source (a quote that cannot be falsified, an elided quote,
and a quote with no attribution).

pdf_text.arxiv:2401.00001:
Grounded Decoding for Scientific Summarisation

Abstract
We study decoding strategies that condition generation on retrieved
passages. The ﬁne-tuned model attains a 12.4–point improvement over
the “closed-book” baseline on our held-out split.

1 Introduction
Summarisation systems that write from parametric memory alone produce
unsupported claims at a rate that grows with the length of the output.
Constraining the decoder to spans present in the retrieved context inter-
national reviewers have called the most direct remedy available today.
 2 Method
Our approach diﬀers from prior work in one respect: the constraint is
applied at every step rather than as a post-hoc ­filter. State-of-the-
art decoding reduces unsupported claims by 41% on the benchmark suite,
and the eﬀect is stable across three seeds.

3 Results
We report a 41% reduction in unsupported claims — the largest eﬀect
we measured​ — without a measurable loss of fluency.
pdf_text.arxiv:2401.00002:
A Survey of Retrieval Augmentation

Abstract
Retrieval augmentation has become the default remedy for factual error
in generated text. We survey forty systems and group them by where the
retrieved context enters the decoder.

1 Scope
The retrieved context provides a form of implicit fact-checking during
generation, and every system we surveyed exploits it in some form.

reports.grounded:
# Grounded decoding

Constrained decoding is the most direct remedy currently available
(arXiv:2401.00001). The authors report that "State-of-the-art decoding
reduces unsupported claims by 41% on the benchmark suite" [Rosen, 2024],
and that the improvement is not bought with fluency.

A quotation broken across a line of the source PDF still resolves: the
introduction argues that constraining the decoder is what
"international reviewers have called the most direct remedy available
today" [Rosen, 2024].

The survey frames the same mechanism differently, describing the
retrieved context as "a form of implicit fact-checking during
generation" [Nair, 2024].

Constrained beam search is treated at length in arXiv:2401.00003, whose
"conditions under which the constraint helps" we do not restate here.
reports.hallucinated:
# Grounded decoding

Constrained decoding is the most direct remedy currently available
(arXiv:2401.00001), and the effect replicates in a later study
(arXiv:2402.99999).

The authors report that "State-of-the-art decoding reduces unsupported
claims by 62% on the benchmark suite" [Rosen, 2024].

They further note that "a form of implicit fact-checking during
generation" is what the constraint provides [Rosen, 2024].

A companion paper is catalogued as arXiv:24x1.0000 in the appendix.
reports.quiet:
# Grounded decoding

Constrained decoding reduces unsupported claims. The effect is stable
across seeds, and it does not cost fluency.
reports.partial_source:
# Grounded decoding

The constrained beam search paper argues that "the constraint is applied
at every step rather than as a post-hoc filter" [Lind, 2024], a framing
this report follows throughout.

The results section reports "a 41% reduction in unsupported claims ...
without a measurable loss of fluency" [Rosen, 2024].

Elsewhere the literature simply asserts that "unsupported claims grow
with the length of the generated output", with no source given at all.
